Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testLANG_831` in FastDateParserTest is failing because FastDateParser treats a single white space in the date format pattern differently from SimpleDateFormat. According to the bug report, SimpleDateFormat's Javadoc does not treat white space specially, but FastDateParser treats a single white space as matching any number of white space characters. This discrepancy causes FastDateParser to parse dates that SimpleDateFormat would reject, leading to inconsistent or incorrect parsing behaviors.

Looking at the code of FastDateParser's parsing mechanism, the key method is `parse(String, ParsePosition)` which uses a compiled regex pattern (`parsePattern`) to match the input date string. This regex pattern is constructed during the initialization (`init()` method). In `init()`, the pattern string is parsed and for each format field a corresponding `Strategy` is obtained and asked to append regex components to the overall regex pattern. The `Strategy` array is then compiled into `parsePattern`.

The root cause of the bug is almost certainly in how the whitespace in the format pattern is translated into regex in these `Strategy` classes when building `parsePattern`. The current implementation allows a single whitespace in the pattern to be matched against any number of whitespace characters, which is more permissive than SimpleDateFormat.

The discrepancy between FastDateParser and SimpleDateFormat parsing behavior can be traced to the regex component generated by the whitespace-related strategy (likely a `SpaceStrategy` or similar) in the pattern compilation step, which is overly permissive and results in mismatched parsing. This causes FastDateParser to accept strings that SimpleDateFormat would reject, leading to test failures.

No evidence from recent bug reports impacts this diagnosis—they relate to other unrelated components or behaviors.

Hence, the bug is caused by an incorrect handling of whitespace in the pattern-to-regex compilation in FastDateParser's init method, specifically in the Strategy class responsible for whitespace handling when building the regex pattern.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
